sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I'm happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Poland.
Poland is a large and historic country in Central Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Poland?
Poland is in Central Europe.
It is next to Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, and the Baltic Sea.
Poland has mountains, forests, lakes, and cities.
What is the capital city of Poland?
The capital city is Warsaw.
Warsaw is a modern city with many offices, parks, museums, and shops.
It was badly damaged in World War II, but it was rebuilt.
Other big cities in Poland include crack off a historic city with a beautiful old town,
Gdansk, a port city by the sea,
Raswa with rivers and bridges,
Pausnine and Wuch important business and culture centers.
How many people live in Poland?
About 38 million people live in Poland.
Most people live in cities or towns.
Some people live in villages or near the countryside.
Poland is part of the European Union, and many Polish people live and work in other countries too.
What language do people speak in Poland?
People in Poland speak Polish.
It is the official language and is used in schools, shops, and government.
Polish is a Slavic language and can be difficult to pronounce.
But many young people also speak English, especially in cities and schools.
What is the weather like in Poland?
Poland has four seasons.
Cool with flowers and green trees.
Summer.
Warm and sunny.
Good for travel.
Autumn.
Colorful leaves and cooler weather.
Winter cold with snow in many places.
In the mountains, it snows a lot.
In the north, near the sea, it is often windy and wet.
What does Poland look like?
Poland has many different landscapes.
Mountains in the south, like the Tatra Mountains,
Flatland and Fields in the center,
Forest with deer, boars, and birds.
Lakes in the north, like in the Missouri and Lake District.
Beaches along the Baltic Sea.
There are also many castles, villages, and historic towns.
What animals live in Poland?
In the wild, you can find Bison, the largest animal in Europe,
Wolves, links, and foxes.
Deer, boars, and hairs.
Swans, eagles, and other birds.
In the forests and parks, people enjoy hiking and bird watching.
What do people eat in Poland?
Polish food is warm filling and often homemade.
People eat potatoes, cabbage, and beets.
Meat, sausages, and chicken.
Soup and bread.
Popular dishes, pierogi, dumplings filled with meat, cheese, or fruit.
Bigos, hunters stew with meat, and sauerkraut.
Jurek, sauerk soup with sausage and egg.
Goombki, cabbage rolls with rice and meat.
Placizimnacana, potato pancakes.
For dessert, punchki, Polish donuts, cernic, cheesecake, or apple pie.
What do people drink in Poland?
People drink tea and coffee, water and fruit juice, milk.
Adults may drink beer or vodka, a traditional drink in Poland.
In winter, they enjoy hot drinks, and in summer, they drink cold compote.
A sweet fruit drink.
What is life like in Poland?
Life in Poland is modern and traditional at the same time.
People go to school, work, and enjoy family time.
In the countryside, people grow food or raise animals.
In cities, people work in offices, shops, or factories.
People enjoy walking in parks, going to cafes, visiting family,
listening to music and reading.
Polish people are known for being kind, hardworking, and proud of their culture.
What are some holidays and traditions in Poland?
Christmas with special food, songs, and decorations.
Easter with painted eggs and church visits.
All Saints Day, November 1, people like candles at graves.
Constitution Day, May 3, Independence Day, November 11.
People also enjoy name days, weddings, and local festivals with music and dancing.
Traditional clothes and folk music are still worn and played in some regions.
Some fun facts about Poland.
Poland has one of the oldest universities in Europe, in Krakow.
The Polish flag is white and red.
The Polish alphabet has 32 letters.
Famous people from Poland include Marie Curie and Frederick Chopin.
Rotswah is known for its tiny gnome statues hidden around the city.
Now you know many things about Poland.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about the cities, weather, traditions, and daily life.
Good job.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.

Go with Zenya.
